content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Summary — TRANSITION: deviation (fallback cure proposed)**

- **What exists:** Section 7.5 (p0343–p0347) gives cooperation "[o]n its resignation or termination" and transfer of the Receivable Files and records; Section 7.3 (p0329) keeps the Servicer performing until a Successor Servicer accepts or the date stated in the termination notice; Section 3.10(f) (p0147) requires custodial file delivery "as soon as practicable."
- **Why it fails fallback:** no minimum assistance period (7.3's tail can be much shorter than 90 days) and no 30-day outside date for delivery of files/records — only an open-ended "as soon as practicable."
- **Cure:** one inserted Section 7.5(d) fixing (i) at least 90 days of transition assistance and (ii) a 30-day backstop for delivery of the Receivable Files and records, measured from the effective date of resignation or termination.
- **Deliberately not raised:** preferred-level machine-readable format and certified deletion (fallback selected); the 7.5(b) carve-back for processes, models and servicing software is left for the IP rule to avoid double-flagging.
